uncertain: Spellblade's Scholar's Armament converts a weapon to Charisma attack and damage, which is worthless on an Int chassis. The dip is priced on Paragon 1's armour, saves and Willpower dice plus Arcana Expertise — a different Heroic Title would score the same here.

Skills is scored one rung below the Expertise-×2 ladder entry in every act because the chassis has no Guidance; Whispers of the Dead substitutes breadth for the cantrip, which the rubric does not price.

The Cunning Strike / Book of Rogues compatibility patch was authored against Book of Rogues 1.0.0.2 and Listo ships 1.0.0.3; the patch author says he did not test the level-17 features. Only Phantom 3 is used here, so the risk is small.

Monster Tactician's Expertise is stated as applying to an Intelligence skill; whether it can be pointed at Religion specifically (the Mirror's check) rather than a fixed pick is not documented. If it is fixed, Act III Skills falls to 3.
Inquisitor's own skill list is not documented, so no Sleight of Hand body is assumed for the Act II Araj gate; Skills is held at 3 in Act II for that reason.
Durability 5 in Act I spends one of the two Act I feats on Heavy Armour Master; the second goes to the Intelligence half-feat, so no damage feat exists before Act II.

Assassinate: Ambush is written as 'any successful attack roll against a Surprised creature is a critical hit'. Whether Listo's implementation fires on spell attack rolls as well as weapon attacks is not confirmed from the pak; if it is weapon-only the Act I single-target 4 falls to 2 and the variant loses most of its point.

Whether Battle Smith's Steel Defender lands at Artificer 3 in this mod is not confirmed — the class file says the subclasses are back-loaded and names Extra Attack at 5 as Battle Smith's payoff. If the Defender is later, Actions falls to 3 in Act II and III.
Artificer's Rounded Up Spellcaster Level passive is documented as working only with core-game spellcasters; the Artificer/Wizard slot stack is core-on-core, so it should hold.

Hexcraft copies Warlock spells into the spellbook as Wizard spells, so Eldritch Blast should key off Intelligence; Agonising Blast adds the Charisma modifier and this body's Charisma is secondary, so the at-will damage is scored a rung below Malison's in Act I.

The mod page places Minor Conjuration's replacement at level 3 while vanilla places it at 2; whether the level-2 slot is replaced or supplemented is unverified, which moves the engine one character level either way.
AoE slides a rung in Act III because the conjured items are flat-magnitude and take their last die step at level 15.
Swashbuckler has no subclass features from 13 to 20, but only three levels are taken here so nothing is stranded.

**Severe.** School of Bombardment's per-level features are published only as images and the mod.io mirror is JavaScript-gated, so every mechanic is unverified. Both this body and Ordnance are therefore the generic Wizard chassis plus a dip, and the pair of rows measures the dip, not the school. A human should read the level-up screen before either row is trusted.
Silver Tongue is keyed on being proficient, so it does not transfer through Use Highest Modifier in dialogue — this body has to be the host.

Sorcery points equal Sorcerer class level, so the dip has three per long rest of its own; the Act I and II readings assume Font of Magic is converting Wizard slots into points every fight rather than living off the three.
Skills sits at 2 in all three acts: Guidance at will is present but Expertise is not, and the ladder's rung 3 requires both. In Act III the absence of any answer to a DC 25 caps it at 2 regardless.

Rescue is held at 3 in all three acts rather than Retort's 4-then-3: the Constitution-save stone is the same handout, but without Cleric 1's Life-domain framing there is no second outward source, and the rubric's rung 4 wants prevention or a per-round aura.

War Magic's per-level numbers — Arcane Deflection, Tactical Wit, Power Surge, Durable Magic — are published only as images and are unverified, so the school contributes nothing to these scores beyond the generic Wizard list, exactly as it does on Vantage.

Agonising Blast is not taken: this chassis's Charisma is secondary, so the two invocations go to Devil's Sight and Armour of Shadows and the Warlock dip is priced purely on slots, the familiar and the saves.

Level order assumed: Fighter 1-3, Rogue 1-5, Fighter 4-7, Rogue 6-11, Fighter 8-9. Brutish Durability therefore lands at character 12, inside Act II.

The Inquisitor multiclass node is undocumented, but Inquisitor is the level-1 class here so only the Rogue side is affected: Rogue as a later class grants light armour and one skill, no Expertise-at-1 and no saves.
Act III AoE falls two rungs because Eldritch Cone stops scaling at character 10 and there is no Consuming Fervor underneath it here.
Aura of Protection is a pair-scope booster and does not stack with a second Aura; if this body is paired with any Paladin 6 the levels behind one of them are wasted.
Level order assumed: Paladin 1-6 at characters 1-6, Warlock 1-14 after. Eldritch Cone therefore lands at character 15, at the very end of Act II, and stops scaling immediately.

Death Ward is a 4th-level spell and arrives with Warlock 7 pact slots at character 10; Twinned costs one sorcery point per slot level, so covering both bodies is a four-point spend against a three-point pool unless Font of Magic has converted a pact slot first.
Twinned Haste is not scored: neither the Archfey expanded list nor a three-level Sorcerer's own known spells reach it.

Auspex: Knowledge domain (Cleric 1 taken first) is read as granting proficiency AND double bonus in Religion; cleric.md says a Cleric multiclass grants no class skills, but the domain grant is a subclass feature and the chassis note names it explicitly. Religion is the whole Act III case for this body.
Clockwork: Artificer 1 grants Sleight of Hand outright (artificer.md line 37), so this body carries the Araj gate skill despite a skl rung of 2. Expertise in it arrives only at Artificer 6, which this split never reaches.
Codex: Six types is deliberate, not padding: Order of Scribes rewrites a spell's damage type on demand and Formulaic Attunement then ignores resistance to the attuned type. This is the one body in the batch with no Absolute Wrath exposure at all.
Conjuration: Read as Rogue-as-level-1 (4 skills + Expertise x2), matching the other 3/4/4 Wizard-Rogue chassis. Only 3 Rogue levels, so no second Expertise pair at Rogue 6 and no Reliable Talent.
Duelist: Bladesong grants advantage on Acrobatics, which is not a modifier and is not folded into the number above; treat the listed Acrobatics as the floor while Bladesong is up.
Grimoire: Bard-as-level-1 with College of Lore at 3: 3 class skills + 3 Lore bonus proficiencies + Expertise x2, spent here on Investigation and Religion. This is the only Wizard chassis in the batch that clears Mirror of Loss on its own numbers.
Interrogator: Two stacked Inquisitor readings: Stern Gaze lets Intimidation run off Wisdom (assumed Wis 14), and Vengeance's Monster Tactician gives Expertise in one Intelligence skill plus half-Wis to every proficient Intelligence skill, taken here as Religion. Religion 17 vs Mirror DC 25 is the best unaided Act III number in the batch. Damage list is wide for the Order of Scribes reason, same as Codex.
Necromancy: The wide skill list is Phantom's Whispers of the Dead, which grants proficiency in every skill of a chosen ability once per short rest. revisions.label: Skills axis rebuilt on untelegraphed checks
revisions.why: Every gated ability-score reward in the run turned out to be obtainable without passing a check, and the hardest gate was buyable with a 100-gold respec.
model_changes: Mirror of Loss REMOVED from the gate table. bg3.wiki documents respeccing at Withers into Rogue 11 / Knowledge Cleric 1 for Religion Expertise, passing DC 25, then respeccing back 'retaining the Mirror of Loss stat enhancement'. Withers is recruitable from the Dank Crypt. Also confirmed per-character ('Each character, including hirelings, may obtain bonuses from the mirror independently'), which would have made it the run's only personal check.
'Gauntlet trap' (Perception DC 15) REMOVED as fabricated — it appears nowhere in references/gates.md and was inflating Act I for 114 of 265 chassis.

Three untelegraphed check classes ADDED, scored every act: traps and hidden caches (Perception 15-25), secret doors and switches (Investigation 15-20), routine town dialogue (Persuasion at the act band 10-15 / 15-18 / 18-22, sourced from listo-10.2-backgrounds.md:104).
Inspiration rerolls restricted to named gates. Traps roll automatically with no prompt, and four charges do not stretch across a run of town dialogue.
Hag's Hair Intimidation DC 15 with advantage restricted to Fighter/Barbarian — it had been offered to every chassis, overstating 87 of 265.

Rung function changed from an all-quantifier to the mean clear probability across the act's checks, capped when the worst check falls below 0.25 (rung<=3) or 0.10 (rung<=2). The all-quantifier put 72-86% of pairs on a single rung.
evidence: Routine-skills sweep, 6 agents, 265 chassis x 3 skills x 3 acts. Persuasion had never been collected (0/265); Perception was on 169/265 and Investigation on 127/265.
77 values disagreed with previously recorded numbers. Every slice showed a scatter rather than a constant offset, so no systematic inter-agent drift.

Repair pass, 2 agents, 27 chassis / 64 falling series in the pre-existing named-gate columns (Sleight of Hand 16, Acrobatics 15, Athletics 15, Deception 9, Intimidation 9). A modifier cannot fall between acts under a rising proficiency bonus; 131 values changed.
Prose pass, 7 agents: 93 roster notes made self-contained, 16 entries rewritten for changed partners or written from scratch.
corrected_briefs: evidence-brief.md gave proficiency bonus as a RANGE ('+2/+3 -> +3/+4 -> +4/+5'), which let one agent use +2/+3/+4 against a consensus of +3/+4/+5 and required 47 chassis to be hand-corrected. Now pinned as exact values with the reason attached.

routine-skills-brief.md initially claimed Knowledge Cleric 1 was 'the common route to Investigation Expertise'. False for this modlist: cleric.md:153 restricts Knowledge Domain Expertise to Arcana/History/Nature/Religion. Caught by an agent, corrected mid-sweep.

backgrounds.md claimed Perception detection is 'passive, never rolled'. bg3.wiki: 'sometimes erroneously referred to as passive perception checks ... in Baldur's Gate 3 they are instead implemented as automatic rolls.' The conclusion (the bank cannot reach it) survives; the mechanism did not.
backgrounds.md called Persuasion 'breadth' because no named gate runs off it. The right test is telegraphed versus not, and town dialogue is the largest untelegraphed load in the run.
known_limitations: Proficiency bonus pinned at +3/+4/+5 by act across all nine recorded skills; strict rules give +6 for characters 17-20. Measured: 15/20 top-20 overlap, max 0.9 score delta, Act III rung changes on 87/265. Systematic rather than scatter. Correcting it means re-deriving all nine skills.

Skills rung 5 is unreachable. Best pair averages 0.79 against a 0.75 threshold, but Perception against the trap band peaks at 0.60 for anyone, and the worst-check cap holds the rung down. The axis runs 0-4 in practice.
64 named-gate falling series were repaired, but the underlying cause in the original evidence pass was never identified — only its signature.
